note: The open spot sheet of Poznan Gr.1181 (units/app5320pozgr1181/intake/spot_rows.py, 2026-10-26), taken over by the Latin audit at the editor's word (2026-11-27, "You can try it"). Each row is read first on the original scan; what the page settles is applied as a row of intake/latin_audit.json, what it does not goes on the audit's one sheet. The two Principles rows are answered in part by the ruling of 2026-11-27 (EDITORIAL_RULES): an ending certain from its sentence is bracketed (Nieszczevicen[sem]), an uncertain one keeps the editor's mark; the 108 withdrawn completions (intake/split_and_settle.py) are not re-applied wholesale but re-derived one by one on the scans.

rows.question: The register heading "4ta Martii" - does a year follow it on the page?
rows.note: The entry records an actum of 29 March 1784 (the weekday formula fits 1784 exactly, and its own narrative says "anno immediate elapso 1783" for the December terminus - the year 1783 now read on the page). If the heading carries a year, it says when the relation was registered.

rows.question: The estate name before "Kanino" - read it ("Termilis"? "Ternilis"?)
rows.note: It stands again on 163v ("Bona Ternilis[?] Kanino Swiątniki et Jaryszki"), disposed of in other hands before 1729. Read the letters.

rows.question: The husband of Victoria in "3tio voto ... Odechowski" - read the word
rows.note: On 164v the same couple stands as "Magnificorum Caroli et Victoriae itidem de Prusimskie Odechowskich conjugum". If the word here is "Michaeli", the two passages disagree and the genealogy follows the better attested one.
